name: On dual consumer RX 7900 XT, tensor parallelism yields only 1.11x-1.23x decode scaling due to KV-head starvation while achieving 1.56x-1.87x prefill scaling
symptom: Adding a second consumer RX 7900 GPU under vLLM TP=2 yields only 1.11x to 1.23x speedup on batch-1 token generation across context lengths from 500 to 32K tokens on dense and MoE models (e.g. 1.13x-1.23x on gemma-4-12B, 1.11x-1.12x on gemma-4-26B-A4B). In contrast, prompt processing (prefill) on the same pair achieves 1.56x to 1.87x wall-clock speedup.
root_cause: The decode scaling bottleneck is not primarily interconnect all-reduce latency over PCIe (which measures only ~1.85 ms out of 16.70 ms per step). Instead, 2D flash-decoding launches one GPU workgroup per KV head; tensor parallelism halves the KV heads per GPU, doubling compute starvation during batch-1 decode. Prefill scales cleanly (1.56x-1.87x) because prompt attention parallelises across attention heads with zero inter-GPU communication.
workaround: Do not scale consumer RDNA3 cards via tensor parallelism expecting 2x batch-1 decode throughput. Use pipeline parallelism, independent model replica serving, or leverage the dual-card setup primarily for larger context/model capacity and prefill throughput gains.
notes: Directly measured by cadamcat on 2x RX 7900 XT in dual-radeon-vllm across eleven ladder depths with verify_doc_figures.py regression checks.
